question.text: According to the NISM Series XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook, which time-based rebalancing frequency is expressly described as the most popular choice for an Indian PMS portfolio?

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Series XXI-B workbook (p.396) lists monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, and annual as recognised time-based rebalancing frequencies for PMS portfolios and expressly identifies quarterly rebalancing as the most popular choice. By narrowing the stem to "expressly described as the most popular choice", quarterly is uniquely correct. The Trap: Daily rebalancing is excessive and not on the workbook's list. "Once every 5 years" is not a recognised time-based frequency under the workbook. "Never" contradicts the very concept of time-based rebalancing. The audit flagged the original because the prior option "Yearly" was also listed by the workbook as a valid frequency, which made the original stem support two answers. Note: The original stem asked the "typical" frequency for a 25-stock PMS without anchoring to what the workbook calls most popular, and the distractor "Yearly" was itself a valid workbook frequency. The stem now asks specifically what the workbook calls the most popular choice, and the "Yearly" distractor has been replaced with "Once every 5 years" (clearly unsupported), making "Quarterly" the uniquely correct answer.
